class.name: LocalLRTVolume3D
class.brief_description: Configures a local LRT diffuse global illumination volume.
class.description: Activation follows [method Node3D.is_visible_in_tree], including ancestor visibility. There is no global or per-volume Enabled switch. Hidden volumes do not inject or propagate lighting, submit geometry rebuilds, blend into surfaces, or supply boundary lighting. Their baked data and per-volume CPU/GPU caches are retained. In-flight geometry jobs may finish, but publication and further submissions pause until shown. On showing, pending geometry changes are processed before the volume supplies lighting again. Remove or free the node to release its runtime caches. Activation is not tied to camera frustum or occlusion culling. Defines a regular probe grid in local space. Translation, rotation and positive uniform scale are supported. The volume is centered on the node origin and edited through [member size], like [VoxelGI]. Drag the six face handles to resize a face, or hold [kbd]Alt[/kbd] to resize symmetrically about the center. Grid snapping, cancel and undo use the standard 3D editor behavior. Probe positions start at -size / 2 and advance by [member probe_spacing]; the final probe on each axis may lie just beyond the bounds to cover a partial cell. Select this node and use [b]Bake LRT Volume[/b] in the 3D toolbar, or call [method bake], to bake visible Static GI mesh instances in the volume and its probe neighborhood. Inside states use the absolute generalized winding number greater than 0.5, allowing open and nonmanifold meshes to contribute locally enclosed regions. Closed manifolds use an equivalent accelerated ray query. Single sheets do not define a solid interior. Dynamic and Disabled GI instances are excluded from the static bake. When this volume is visible in the scene tree, CPU workers rebuild 8×8×8-probe trunks affected by Dynamic GI MeshInstance3D and MultiMeshInstance3D nodes with [LRTGeometryBinding] metadata, configured through Global Illumination > LRT in the Inspector. Instance movement, visibility, GI mode, bindings and baked-resource changes invalidate affected trunks. The global rendering/global_illumination/lrt/geometry_trunks_per_frame budget limits submissions across all volumes. Ready trunks are packed on workers and published independently through [signal geometry_updated], without waiting for the full dirty region. Old and new instance bounds are marked separately and deduplicated. A bounded in-flight batch finishes while pending changes are coalesced in FIFO order; in-flight work is never exposed through [method get_geometry_trunk]. Completed trunks are queued to the rendering thread as GPU scatter uploads. Each shared Edge has one canonical owner that updates both endpoints; uploads from its non-owning endpoint cannot overwrite it. Replacing a static baseline first recomposes its dynamic snapshot on a worker and publishes the complete result together, while retaining the previous published CPU/GPU cache during computation. Each changed probe updates its packed geometry and fixed emission. Probes outside solids both before and after the update preserve both L/A propagation histories and continue converging under the new geometry. Inside probes clear both histories; probes newly exposed from Inside initialize both histories to L=0, A=LocalVis. Full volume resets initialize all histories. Geometry uploads do not overwrite untouched probes; normal propagation continues to update them. Removing the volume or blocking CPU geometry releases its GPU buffers; hiding it retains them. GPU lighting and surface sampling require the Forward+ renderer; unsupported renderers report a blocked GPU status rather than substituting another GI path. After shadow rendering, each ready volume propagates global visibility A, injects direct light, visible sky and fixed emission as S=T(Ddirect+B)+J, and then propagates L using 26 neighbors, shared Edge masks, decoded LocalVis/LTM, FP32 ping-pong buffers. Each iteration directly writes the newly computed result. Directional, Omni and Spot lights with Static or Dynamic bake mode are collected from the world. Injection uses linear, unexposed colors, indirect energy, range/cone attenuation and current shadow maps. Shadowed positional lights without available current shadow data are not injected; directional lights outside shadow coverage use propagated A. Environment ambient source, color, energy, sky contribution and sky rotation produce world-space Sky SH. Each world updates once per runtime frame using the first rendered view of that world. rendering/global_illumination/lrt/propagation_iterations controls the iteration count for each field per frame. Inside probes remain zero. Each iteration reads only the previous buffer; barriers separate dependent passes. Volumes update from lower to higher priority, with instance ID as a stable tie-breaker. Out-of-grid neighbors sample the highest-priority ready lower-priority volume covering that world position and rotate SH into the current volume. Boundary interpolation includes Inside zero states and ignores display intensity and coverage. With no supplier, boundaries are open (A=SH_ONE, L=0). [b]Development status:[/b] Forward+ direct Probe sampling is available when rendering/global_illumination/lrt/screen_gather_enabled is false. Surface sampling offsets the lookup position along the world-space unit surface normal by the receiving instance's [member LRTGeometryBinding.surface_normal_bias], or rendering/global_illumination/lrt/surface_normal_bias (default 0.1 meters) when inherited. The offset is independent of probe spacing and node scale. Sampling interpolates eight Probes after excluding Inside samples, uses identical normalized weights for L and A, and does not query Edge visibility. It reconstructs indirect irradiance/pi and blends with original ambient lighting before material color and AO. Volume coverage and edge blending use the original, unshifted surface position. With a positive valid trilinear weight sum, coverage depends only on volume edge blending and is not attenuated by the weight sum. With no valid samples, the volume is skipped. Losing the last valid contribution can cause an abrupt transition to lower-priority volumes or original ambient lighting. Excessive bias can lose contact detail or cross narrow geometry. With no active ready volume, surfaces use original ambient lighting. With rendering/global_illumination/lrt/screen_gather_enabled enabled, each viewport requests a normal/depth prepass and builds a premultiplied HDR lighting/coverage cache at scale 1, 0.5 or 0.25, followed by depth/normal-guided upsampling. Transparent passes and unmatched surfaces use direct Probe sampling. The normal/depth prepass additionally writes an R16F per-pixel surface bias. MSAA resolve selects bias from the same sample as depth and normal, and upsampling excludes representatives with a different bias. View caches encode camera exposure once before FP16 storage to preserve HDR range; world propagation and boundary inputs remain unexposed. Sky uses an additional unexposed material output without changing the original Godot sky cache. Display Advanced provides nine LRT views: gathered indirect lighting, direct Probe sampling, propagated Probe lighting, local visibility, global visibility, Edge visibility, static LTM, Color SDF and Trunk updates. Select a Volume to isolate it or a GeometryInstance3D to display its Color SDF. Diagnostics and legends are shown directly in the viewport. Material support is the same as [LRTGeometryBinding].

method.name: inspect_probe
method.description: Reconstructs the selected probe's 26 current geometry queries for diagnostics. Returns point, coordinate, samples and the published cache revision when available. Each sample reports position, hit, albedo, emission and the shared four-bit edge_mask; supplied boundary neighbors also report boundary_volume, boundary_index and boundary_direction_in_source. Static queries build a BVH of current scene geometry; dynamic queries use current instance snapshots. These queries may differ from the published cache during pending rebuilds or after unbaked static edits. This is a synchronous diagnostic operation, not a normal per-frame rendering API.

method.name: bake
method.description: Starts an explicit asynchronous static bake using the same core in the editor and at runtime. Searches [param from_node], or the current scene (edited scene in the editor) when null. Scene input is captured in bounded main-thread steps; material readback, geometry, Probe and Edge generation execute asynchronously. Successful completion atomically assigns the finished [member bake_data]; failure or cancellation preserves the previous result. No file is required or saved. Use the returned [LRTBakeTask] for progress, cancellation, resource issues and completion. Saving through [ResourceSaver] is a separate operation.

method.name: get_bounds
method.description: Returns the local-space coverage AABB, centered on the node origin with dimensions [member size].

method.name: get_geometry_status
method.description: Returns CPU geometry scheduling diagnostics. state is disabled, pending, updating, ready, failed or blocked. A failed CPU task reports its error and retains the last valid published cache, when ready is true; it does not retry every frame. Hide and show the volume or assign different bake_data to retry. ready indicates a published dynamic snapshot is available, which may be older than a currently computing batch. Active states include revision, pending_trunks, computing_trunks, cached_trunks, last_submitted_trunks, last_changed_trunks, cpu_task_usec (cumulative rebuild and packing worker time), published_trunks (local trunk publications), last_result_age_usec (snapshot-to-CPU-publication age, including index/worker queueing but excluding later render-thread/GPU delay) and error. frame_submitted_trunks counts submissions across all volumes during the current runtime frame. A blocked volume cannot supply geometry. The gpu subdictionary reports pending, ready or blocked, with the last render-thread-committed revision, grid_size, updated_probes, allocated_bytes and optional error. A ready GPU revision means its commands precede subsequent render work, not that the GPU has finished execution. After propagation, gpu also includes propagation_frame (runtime frame of the last dispatch), propagation_steps (total A and L passes since the full baseline reset), propagation_iterations and history_index (latest ping-pong buffer). injected_lights reports the number of collected light inputs and surface_sampling indicates that the direct-sampling buffers were prepared. cpu_submit_usec measures propagation/injection command submission. gpu_usec and gpu_timing_frame report delayed GPU timestamp measurements for those passes, not whole-frame overhead. gather_size, gather_bytes, gather_cpu_usec, gather_gpu_usec and gather_timing_frame describe the latest rendered view. sampling_bytes reports world-shared geometry/history/metadata storage, sky_cache_bytes reports the optional unexposed sky cache, and debug_bytes reports optional direct-light diagnostics. CPU worker time is cumulative. Normal status queries do not synchronize or read back the GPU. GPU failures discard the cache and require a full baseline reset (for example, reassign bake_data or hide and show the volume).

method.name: get_geometry_gpu_trunk
method.description: Synchronously reads one trunk back from the GPU for diagnostics. This stalls rendering and must not be used in normal per-frame rendering. Returns coordinate, origin, size, revision, ltm, local_vis, edge_masks, emission (12 FP32 coefficients per probe, including zeros when absent), light_0/light_1 (12 FP32 coefficients per probe) and visibility_0/visibility_1 (4 FP32 coefficients per probe). Also returns source (12 FP32 S coefficients per probe, empty before light injection), sky (12 world-space Sky SH coefficients when available), history_index, propagation_frame and propagation_steps; use history_index to select the latest L/A state. The other history buffer can contain the preceding iteration. Returns an error field when GPU data is unavailable or the coordinate is invalid. Call on the main thread. GPU storage uses 72 bytes of aligned packed geometry, 48 bytes of fixed emission, 48 bytes of injected source S and two 64-byte L/A histories per probe (296 bytes total). Direct surface sampling additionally maintains 136 bytes per probe in a world-shared GPU geometry/history copy, 128 bytes per volume of metadata, a 64-byte metadata header and 48 bytes of Sky SH. allocated_bytes reports only the per-volume propagation buffers, excluding world-shared sampling buffers, transient light inputs/staging, shaders and driver allocation overhead. Optional direct-light diagnostics use another 64 bytes per probe. View caches additionally use an R16F surface-bias pixel per full-resolution pixel (and a matching multisample attachment when MSAA is enabled). Lighting and guide caches use 24 bytes per full-resolution and low-resolution pixel (FP16 lighting/coverage plus FP32 position/normal guide). The optional unexposed Sky material cache uses FP32 RGB(A) with three mip levels, preserving values beyond FP16 range.

method.name: get_geometry_trunk
method.description: Returns the last published CPU geometry for a zero-based trunk coordinate. Fields are coordinate, origin (probe grid coordinate), size (at most 8 per axis), ltm, local_vis, edge_masks, emission, instances (instance IDs in stable order), and revision. Channel layouts match [LocalLRTVolumeData], with x-fastest samples within the trunk. Untouched trunks use the static bake. Requires a ready, unblocked published cache; never returns worker-owned in-flight data. During a same-layout static replacement it continues returning the previous published cache until the complete replacement is ready. Returned arrays are independent copy-on-write values.

method.name: get_grid_size
method.description: Returns ceil(size / probe_spacing) + 1 on each axis, including the boundary probes.

members.member: Static geometry cache for this volume. Changes to size, spacing, static geometry or materials require rebaking.
Width of the final display blend at the volume boundary, measured in probe cells.
Nonnegative display intensity, applied before volume blending, not to propagated boundary light.
Lower-priority volumes supply boundary lighting to higher-priority volumes. Higher priority also takes precedence in final blending.
Positive probe spacing in local meters. A carriage typically uses 0.25 meters.
Local-space volume dimensions in meters, centered on the node origin. All dimensions must be positive. Use the node transform to position and rotate the volume.

signal.name: geometry_updated
signal.description: Emitted on the main thread after publishing ready CPU geometry results. Read changed trunks with [method get_geometry_trunk]. When reset is true, a complete initial, layout-reset or static replacement cache, already composed with its dynamic snapshot, is available. The flag describes replacement of CPU geometry, not resetting air-probe lighting: a same-layout static replacement preserves those histories. Shared Edge masks at both endpoints change in the same GPU dispatch, even if the adjacent trunk has not completed. Further instance changes during worker execution are retained for a later batch. The corresponding GPU scatter upload and required history initialization for layout changes or Inside-transition probes have been queued before this signal. Light injection and propagation happen later during Forward+ rendering, not during this notification. CPU notification does not wait for the rendering thread or GPU; compare the gpu revision in [method get_geometry_status] when inspecting upload progress.
